title: Sessions vs JWT: Python Web Auth

scenes.say: Sessions or JWT for authentication? What's the real difference and why does it matter?

scenes.label: Session
scenes.sub: User state is stored on the server, tracked by a cookie.
scenes.say: Session authentication keeps user state on the server and tracks it with a cookie.

scenes.label: JWT
scenes.sub: User info is encoded in a signed token sent with each request.
scenes.say: JWT is stateless. User info is packed in a signed token and sent every time.
Session means the server remembers you. JWT means the server checks your token but doesn't save your state.

scenes.question: Which is more scalable for APIs?
scenes.right: JWT is more scalable since it's stateless and doesn't need server storage.
scenes.say: Which is more scalable for APIs? It's JWT, because stateless tokens don't need server storage.
